answer: Each agent may reserve only one ingress channel per real-world payment instrument, and must lock a deposit that refunds solely if that instrument opens no second channel for six epochs. Mid-window, at the zenith of traffic, auditors stitch those channels into a river of settlement traces. Keys fed by the same instrument are treated as one vine: extra deposits are burned rather than refunded, and only the first channel keeps its weight. A factory of aliases therefore needs a new instrument and a fresh locked deposit for every name, so copied keys consume capital instead of multiplying votes.
